title: Generics, Wildcards (PECS) & Type Erasure
subtitle: Master Java Generics type invariance, bounded wildcards (? extends T vs ? super T), the PECS design rule, and bytecode Type Erasure with synthetic bridge methods.
mentalModel: Generics exist strictly at compile time for type safety. Invariance prevents heap pollution; PECS (Producer Extends, Consumer Super) grants flexible read/write permissions; Type Erasure strips generic types in bytecode.

failureModes: Heap Pollution & Unchecked Cast Warnings: Mixing raw types (`List list = new ArrayList()`) with generic types leads to runtime ClassCastException when unexpected objects are retrieved from the collection.
Cannot Create Generic Arrays: Code like `T[] arr = new T[10]` is illegal because array types are reified at runtime while generic types are erased at compile time.
tradeOffs: Wildcard Flexibility vs Type Exactness: Using `List<? extends T>` allows accepting `List<Dog>` or `List<Cat>`, but forbids adding elements to the list.
theoryData.productionScenario: In enterprise framework design (Spring Data Repositories, Kafka Producer/Consumer abstractions), using PECS (`public void ingestAll(Collection<? extends Event> events)`) allows consumer microservices to accept any subclass event payload without compiler type incompatibility errors.

interviewQA.q: What is the difference between `List<Object>` and `List<?>` (Unbounded Wildcard)?
interviewQA.a: `List<Object>` can only accept an exact `List<Object>` (it cannot accept `List<String>`). `List<?>` is an unbounded wildcard that can hold a reference to a list of ANY type (`List<String>`, `List<Integer>`, etc.), but elements read from it are typed as `Object` and no elements (except null) can be added.

interviewQA.q: What is a Synthetic Bridge Method in Java Generics?
interviewQA.a: When a generic class overrides a method from a parameterized superclass/interface, Type Erasure changes the superclass method signature to `method(Object)`. The compiler automatically injects a synthetic 'bridge method' with the `Object` signature in the subclass that delegates to the specialized typed method, preserving polymorphic overriding.

quizData.question: If you have `List<? extends Number> list`, can you execute `list.add(10)`?
quizData.answer: No! `? extends Number` represents an unknown subtype of Number (e.g. `List<Double>`). Adding an Integer (10) would violate type safety, so the compiler prohibits adding anything other than null.

quizData.question: Are generic type parameters available at runtime via standard object inspection (e.g., `list.getClass()`)?
quizData.answer: No. Due to Type Erasure, `ArrayList<String>.class` and `ArrayList<Integer>.class` are both erased to `ArrayList.class` at runtime.
